lesson_title: The Relationship Between Surface Area and Volume
hook_text: Same soap, same twelve bars — and one carton needs half the cardboard of the other.
clip_script:
A small soap factory in Pinetown packs its bars twelve to a cardboard carton for delivery to shops. Each bar is 9 by 6 by 3 centimetres. All twelve in a row make a carton 108 centimetres long — and 1 980 square centimetres of card.

Stack them two along, two across and three high: 18 by 12 by 9. Same twelve bars, same volume, but only 972 square centimetres of card — less than half. Packing compactly hides faces against each other. For a fixed volume, the most cube-like box has the least surface.
visual_style: Twelve soap bars slide from a long row into a compact block; the cardboard net for each carton unfolds beside it, the second visibly half the size
